# Śākyamuni: the restoration, the temple, and the world it opens
The domain you're reading about exists because someone refused to let **Śākyamuni** stay *shakyamuni*.

The life of Śākyamuni is the best-attested sacred biography of the ancient world — told in the Pāli Nikāyas, versified by Aśvaghoṣa, expanded in the Nidānakathā and the Lalitavistara, and anchored in the ground by Aśoka's own inscriptions. Queen Māyā, traveling to her father's house, gave birth standing in the grove at Lumbinī, holding the branch of a sāla tree; the child took seven steps and declared this his last birth.  The legends multiplied — the shower of blossoms, the two streams of water, the prophecy of the sage Asita — but the place is fixed in stone: Aśoka's pillar at Rummindei, raised in his twentieth regnal year, reads in plain Prakrit, hida budhe jāte sakyamuni — "here the Buddha Śākyamuni was born.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Śākyamuni
- **ASCII form:** shakyamuni
- **Meaning:** "‘sage of the Śākya clan’, epithet of the historical Buddha Siddhārtha Gautama, MW."
- **Domain of influence:** Enlightenment, Teaching, Historical Buddha
- **Pantheon:** Buddhist
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** शाक्यमुनि
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 218 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

The name is attested as **शाक्यमुनि**. On the evidence, it means "‘sage of the Śākya clan’, epithet of the historical Buddha Siddhārtha Gautama, MW.".

Strip **Śākyamuni** to *shakyamuni* and one piece of evidence vanishes:

- **a → ā** — Macron: long /aː/: the vowel length the ASCII form cannot show.

A reader who knows the marks hears the name correctly on the first try. A reader who never sees them never gets the chance.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Śākyamuni** lives at [/sites/shakyamuni/](/sites/shakyamuni/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/shakyamuni/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/shakyamuni/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/shakyamuni/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Śākyamuni** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Education, Research & Knowledge** — The teacher of the path; forty-five years of turning the wheel.
- **Faith & Spiritual Organizations** — The founder; the tradition begins under his tree.
- **Yoga, Meditation & Holistic Wellness** — The source of meditation; the mindfulness economy traces every breath to his seat under the tree.

The mapping is conservative on purpose: only resonances that can be argued aloud. The rest of the atlas follows the same rule, industry by industry.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Buddhist tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Lotus Sutra](/texts/lotus-sutra/) and [Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtras](/texts/sukhavativyuha/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
## The File Continues

This is one of 271 Restoration Files — a second dispatch from every flagship temple in the fleet. The temple's [first dispatch](/sites/shakyamuni/blog/) tells the founding story of the name; the [blog index](/blog/) holds the whole archive.

Continue the series — previous file: **Sšꜣt** ([read it here](/sites/seshat/blog/restoration/)) · next file: **Šamaš** ([read it here](/sites/shamash/blog/restoration/)).

*The Restoration Files are written from the same canonical record as the temples themselves: the lexicon, the lore catalog, the pattern atlas, and the cited scholarly sources. If a file ever disagrees with its temple, the temple is right — tell us, and the file will be corrected.*
